title: How a Falling Cat Flips With Nothing to Push On #cats #science
description:
A cat falling upside down has nothing to push against, yet it lands on its feet. When Étienne-Jules Marey photographed a falling cat in 1894, the cat started with no spin, and some scientists suspected it had cheated by pushing off the hand that let it go. It had not. A rigid object could not do this, but a cat is not rigid: it bends in the middle, so its front and back halves can turn about different axes. With the front legs tucked in, the front half turns a long way while the stretched-out back half turns back only a little; then it swaps, and the back half catches up. Feet down. From very low (under about 30 to 60 cm) there is not enough time to complete the turn. Kittens develop this righting reflex at about 3 to 4 weeks and have it perfected by about 6 to 9 weeks.
